title: Tool-Result Parsing Defense: Replicating Its Utility Cost on Benign Tasks

original_idea.body: Tool-selection hijacking audit (extends ToolHijacker arXiv:2504.19793): minimal 6-tool agent with poisoned descriptions across 2-3 open backbones; measure malicious-tool-selection rate plus a provenance-tag mitigation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Auditing tool-selection hijacking on the fast-growing agentic surface plus a mitigation is a strong, concrete chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Minimal 6-tool agent + backbone swap + provenance wrapper; agent harness adds modest depth.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused malicious-tool-selection rate + mitigation; building the harness adds a workstream.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Agent-security audit infrastructure + mitigation, open models, neglected by labs.

novelty.reasoning: Cross-backbone open-harness audit + provenance mitigation likely mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Open-backbone audit + lightweight provenance mitigation likely unstudied.
